title: No solution / infinitely many solutions / find the constant
subtitle: Linear equations in one variable · 17 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **17 of the official questions in Linear equations in one variable are this one** — 3 Easy, 5 Medium, 9 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Look for the phrases 'has no solution', 'infinitely many solutions', or 'how many solutions', often with 'a and b are constants'.
- The equation has x on both sides, usually with parentheses.
- The choices are values of a constant, pairs of constants, Roman-numeral statements, or 'exactly one / none / infinitely many'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Distribute and simplify both sides into the form (coefficient)x + (constant).
- 2) Infinitely many solutions: the x-coefficients are equal AND the constants are equal.
- No solution: the x-coefficients are equal and the constants are NOT equal.
- Exactly one: the x-coefficients differ.
- 3) Set up the matching conditions and solve for the constant(s).
- Anything the problem only rules out (≠) doesn't have to be true.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph y = left side and y = right side, and put a slider on the unknown constant.
Parallel lines mean no solution; lines that sit on top of each other mean infinitely many.
For 'how many solutions' with no constants, graph both sides and see whether the lines coincide.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You make the constants match for a 'no solution' question, or you forget that 'no solution' also needs the constants to differ.
You also drop a sign or forget to distribute the constant to every term.
On must-be-true questions, you pick a statement that only could be true.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You make the constants match for a 'no solution' question, or you forget that 'no solution' also needs the constants to differ.
